title: introduce-federated-anomaly-attenuator-rollout-guard
author: Maya Patel
description:
Summary: Adds a federated anomaly attenuator and an associated rollout guard that reduces false-positive-driven rollbacks by attenuating noisy cohort-level signals and combining them with stable global baselines. This is targeted at canary evaluations that span noisy traffic slices (eg: region, customer cohort, device type) where single-slice spikes trigger unnecessary rollbacks.

Motivation and context: We routinely see spurious canary regressions caused by high-variance slices (small customer cohorts, bursty regional traffic) that lead to overly conservative rollbacks. Existing ensemble detectors tend to amplify short-lived slice noise by treating slices equally. This PR implements an attenuation layer that: (1) dampens high-variance slice signals using a federated variance-aware factor, (2) fuses attenuated slice signals with a global smoothed baseline, and (3) exposes a safety leash (attenuation-factor bounds + cooldown) so attenuation cannot mask true regressions. The goal is fewer false rollbacks while retaining sensitivity to real regressions that manifest across multiple cohorts.

What changed (high level):
- New federated attenuator component and orchestration glue (python + go) that computes per-slice attenuation_factors and a fused canary score.
- New rollout guard policy that uses attenuated scores + quorum rules and an attenuation safety leash to gate automated rollouts.
- Deterministic simulator and e2e canary scenario tests to validate behavior on synthetic bursty traffic.
- New dashboards and playbook additions describing how the attenuator behaves and how to tune attenuation bounds.

Design notes:
- Attenuation algorithm: per-slice attenuation_factor = 1 / (1 + lambda * normalized_variance) where lambda is tunable per-metric. The attenuated slice contribution is factor * slice_delta. Factors are clipped to [min_factor, max_factor] to implement the safety leash.
- Federation: we aggregate slice stats (count, mean, variance) at the probe layer and compute factors locally per-region/agent, then reduce to a global fused score with weighted averaging where weight = slice_traffic^0.75 to soften tiny cohorts.
- Rollout guard policy: requires (a) fused attenuated delta above threshold AND (b) quorum: at least 2 independent regions reporting sustained signal or a global un-attenuated delta > hard_threshold. The policy includes a cooldown window (5m default) and an auto-expiry for attenuation overrides.

Testing done:
- Unit tests for attenuation math and factor clipping (tests/attenuator/test_attenuation.py).
- Integration tests for aggregator and federation code (tests/aggregator/test_federation.go).
- E2E canary simulator scenarios: bursty small-cohort spike, multi-region slow drift, and coordinated regression. Verified: attenuator reduces false positives on single-cohort spikes and preserves detection for coordinated regressions.
- Benchmarked CPU overhead on canary controllers: median +3.1% CPU, 95th +6% on small controllers; identified and optimized hot path in metrics aggregation.

Migration/operational notes:
- Feature is behind feature flag: perf.canary.federated_attenuator (default off in prod).
- Default attenuation parameters are conservative (min_factor=0.35, max_factor=1.0, lambda=0.9).
- Added observability: attenuation_factor per-slice metric, fused_attenuated_score, and attenuation_clipped_count. Dashboards introduced under perf-canary -> Attenuator.

Checklist: 
- [x] Core algorithm implementation
- [x] Unit + integration + e2e tests
- [x] Dashboards + playbook
- [x] Feature flag + safe defaults
- [x] Perf smoke tests

Related Linear/Jira: ENG-1187, ENG-1249

Notes for reviewers: Focus on federation reduction correctness, safety-leash bounds, and whether the quorum rules are conservative enough. The implementation includes thorough comments and a small performance optimization patch in the aggregator that reduces memory churn.

review_conversation: Amit Rao: Nice design. Concern: lambda tuning per-metric may hide regressions for tail P95. Can we add metric-specific guard that disables attenuation above a metric-specific hard_threshold?
Maya Patel: Good point — added hard_threshold check in rollout guard and documented recommended thresholds per metric. See commit 2b3c4d.
Laura Gómez: Tests look good. Request: add an integration test where tiny cohorts are adversarial (alternating spikes) to ensure attenuation doesn't introduce oscillation.
Maya Patel: Added adversarial cohort sim in tests/e2e and extended cooldown window to 5m to prevent oscillation. See commit 3c4d5e.
Devon Chen: Can we keep the default min_factor conservative (0.35)? Also confirm metrics exports are tagged with region and cohort for traceability.
Maya Patel: Kept min_factor=0.35 and added region/cohort labels to attenuation metrics. Updated dashboards to surface clipped counts.
Amit Rao: Approve after small nits addressed.
Devon Chen: Approved and merged via squash.
release_notes: Adds a federated anomaly attenuator and a conservative rollout guard to reduce false-positive canary rollbacks from noisy small cohorts. Feature is behind a feature flag and off by default. Includes dashboards and e2e sims.
